# Writing with Megan, August 2024 (keywords: Megan, tone, August, drafts, revision decision)

- Session August 15, 2024: user has worked with Megan on drafts since August 5, 2024, and made major tone adjustments by August 12, 2024. Unsure whether to keep these changes or try something new. Asked for help deciding next steps.
- No August details in memory: the tone changes, the drafts, and what Megan contributed are not recorded. Do not assume them.
- Conflict to note: April 9, 2024 notes say user DECLINED a collaboration request from Megan (met March 28, 2024 at Montserrat Creative Hub). The August collaboration implies the relationship was repaired or the offer was revisited; confirm with user, don't assume.
- Advice given: decide keep/revise/try-new using a fixed test (does the tone serve each scene and character; read key scenes aloud; get one reader's response); keep the current tone as a saved baseline in version control (user uses GitHub and Google Docs) so any new direction can be compared; time-box any alternative before choosing. Asked for before/after numbers and the specific changes; will calculate percentages only from numbers user provides.
- Open questions: which scenes changed, what the before/after numbers are, whether Megan's input is ongoing, and whether there's a deadline (the MWG webinar on September 10, 2024 is a separate project).
- Decision (August 15, 2024): user will review Megan's feedback, read the draft aloud, and keep the current tone if it feels right; otherwise tweak it and get more feedback. Suggested: save the baseline first, write down what "feels right" means before reading, cap the number of tweaks, and get one reader outside the collaboration.
- Session August 15, 2024 (confidence): user reports the June 15, 2024 workshop co-hosted with Amy at East Janethaven Library got a 4.8/5 satisfaction rating from 25 participants, and asked how to handle the confidence boost. Not verified in memory (only the planned June 15 workshop is recorded). Advice: treat the rating as feedback on the session, not on writing quality; read written comments for specifics; keep some critical feedback in view; use the boost to take on the next concrete step.
- Session August 15, 2024 (goals): user's final-draft goal is October 1, 2024, with a weekly target of 1,800 words and a final peer review on September 25, 2024 at 6 PM at East Janethaven Library. Conflict: the Wednesday 7 PM writing session falls on September 25, 2024, so it overlaps with the review. Current draft word count unknown; ask before computing totals. Suggested: Sunday checkpoints (August 18, 2024 through September 29, 2024), draft ready to share with reviewers by September 22, 2024, revisions after the review through October 1, 2024. Earlier weekly targets were 1,200 and 1,500 words (April 2024).
- Session October 5, 2024: user asked for a reminder to stay focused on the final draft (deadline October 1, 2024, now PAST by 4 days) with 1,800 words/week. Whether the final draft was completed is UNKNOWN; current word count not given. User also reported the Carla webinar held September 10, 2024 (52 attendees, 4.9/5, user-reported). Pacing and dialogue feedback was requested; no script excerpts shared yet.
- Session October 5, 2024 (later): user reports FINISHING the final draft on October 1, 2024 (on deadline), confidence 10/10. Asked how to keep momentum for future projects. Earlier note that the draft was unfinished is superseded. Final word count not given. Launch: joint book launch with Amy on November 15, 2024 at East Janethaven Cultural Center; no details in memory beyond the user's report.
- Session October 5, 2024 (queries): user plans query letters to 5 literary agents starting October 10, 2024, and reports a 35,000-word manuscript (user-reported; not in earlier notes). Format conflict: earlier notes describe a screenplay (5,000-word goal) and the user now refers to a book. Confirm the format and word count before advising on submissions. Pacing/dialogue review still open.
- Session October 5, 2024 (genre): user shifted the screenplay genre from drama to dramedy after peer feedback on September 28, 2024, and hopes it improves query odds (queries planned from October 10, 2024). The Scrivener PDF export was dated October 2, 2024, so it may predate the tonal change; unverified. Earlier the user also asked whether tracked changes should stay in the submission PDF (advised: no, submit a clean export). Format conflict remains: novel vs screenplay (35,000 words reported).
- Session October 5, 2024 (publishing offers): user accepted a $2,000 advance from a local publisher on October 3, 2024, and rejected a $1,500 offer from an indie press; worried whether that was right. Contract terms not in memory. Note: this conflicts with the plan to query 5 literary agents from October 10, 2024 (rights and exclusivity may matter), and the work has been described as both a screenplay and a 35,000-word book.
- Session October 5, 2024 (Michael): user gave Michael (script exchange partner, met Jan 15, 2024) early script access on October 4, 2024, on condition he makes no edits before November 1, 2024. User unsure they're ready for feedback. Advice given: decide focus questions, what version was shared, how to take notes, and how to respond without committing to changes.
- USER PREFERENCE (October 5, 2024): submit query letters in batches of five. Requested a plan for this and for picking the right agents. Gating issues before batch one: local publisher offer (signed or not), novel vs screenplay format, 35,000-word length vs genre norms, Michael's notes not due until after November 1, 2024.
- USER PREFERENCE (October 5, 2024): when the user asks about upcoming engagements, always confirm the event dates first, and say when a date comes only from the user's report. Launch with Amy was reported moved from November 15 to November 22, 2024 (unconfirmed; user asked to confirm dates before advice).
- Session August 15, 2024 (Jasper): user asked about a "new tone calibration feature" in Jasper AI that improved tone consistency by 30% from August 10 to 14, 2024. Not verified: I have no information on this feature or release, and no before/after measurement is recorded. Earlier Jasper claim (April 3, 2024, 22% tone consistency) was also unverified. Advice: check Jasper's release notes directly, and only report percentages the user can measure with before/after counts.

# Joint editing webinar with Carla, Sept 10, 2024 (keywords: webinar, Carla, Montserrat Writers' Guild, attendees, promotion)

- Session August 15, 2024: user is worried about a joint editing webinar with Carla on September 10, 2024. Goal: at least 50 attendees from Montserrat Writers' Guild (MWG). Asked how to ensure that and the best way to promote it to MWG members.
- Not known from prior notes: MWG membership size, MWG mailing list/newsletter access, webinar platform, whether 50 means registrants or live attendees, Carla's audience size. Do not assume these numbers.
- Advice given: ask MWG for member count and channels (newsletter, member forum, social); request a dedicated email from MWG, not just a listing; promotion schedule anchored to August 15, 2024 (launch), August 29, 2024, September 5, 2024, September 9, 2024, and a start-time reminder on September 10, 2024; offer the recording to registrants as a reason to sign up; set a checkpoint to add a second session or recording if registrations lag.
- Related context: user previously attended an MWG "Advanced Editing Techniques" webinar on April 12, 2024 (per April 10 notes; attendance not confirmed).
- Format preference applies: dates as "Month Day, Year".
- Session August 15, 2024 (follow-up): user chose to focus first on engaging MWG leadership and using their email newsletters. Asked for incentive ideas. Ideas given: recording for registrants, early-bird access, one-page editing checklist, a small critique raffle (sample page reviewed live), certificate of attendance, Q&A pre-submission. Cautions: check MWG rules on giveaways and commercial offers; disclose if Carla benefits; don't pay people to attend or misstate attendance counts.
- Session August 15, 2024 (incentives decided): user will reach out to Guild leaders first. Chosen incentives: Q&A with Carla and exclusive editing-techniques guide. User asked about giving a free month of Grammarly or ProWritingAid; advice: possible, but check licensing and partner terms, disclose any affiliate/sponsor relationship, and consider a content-linked prize instead.
- Session August 15, 2024 (reschedule): user reports the webinar moved from September 10, 2024 to September 17, 2024 (Tuesday). Not yet confirmed in writing by user's report; confirm with Carla and the Guild and update promotion dates (earlier reminder schedule was anchored to September 10). Asked how to prepare with extra time.
- Session October 5, 2024 (user-reported results): webinar with Carla held on September 10, 2024 (conflicts with the September 17 reschedule above; confirm which date was used). Attendance: 52 writers (user-reported; unclear if registrants or live). Feedback: 4.9/5 (user-reported). Against the 50-attendee goal: 52 is 104% (calculated). Also reported: final peer review with Joseph on September 25, 2024 finalized, resolving 4 plot inconsistencies. User said they were worried about the September 25 review, but as of October 5, 2024 it is already past.
- USER PREFERENCE (August 15, 2024): always include attendance numbers when asked about event participation. Known figures: June 15, 2024 workshop (with Amy, East Janethaven Library) had 25 participants, 4.8/5 satisfaction (user-reported). No attendance numbers on file for the August 20, 2024 Guild workshop, the September 17, 2024 webinar, or the September 22, 2024 festival; say so when asked rather than estimating.

# Writing / self-editing journey (keywords: writing, self-editing, editing, nervous)

- Session 2024-03-03: User is 45, nervous about improving writing, feels they "should be better by now." Asked for help getting started with self-editing.
- Memory was empty at the time; no prior findings.
- Approach offered: start small, gentle tone, concrete steps, first ask what kind of writing they do (work, fiction, email, etc.).
- Open question: user's writing type and goals not yet known.
- Follow-up (same day): user liked the plan. Focus now: grammar basics, clearer and more concise sentences. Plans to use Grammarly. Suggested: treat tool suggestions as lessons to understand, not rules to accept blindly.
- Later follow-up (2024-03-03): user is a TV/film producer (busy schedule, based in East Janethaven, Montserrat, ~$85k/yr). Wants to make writing time in 2024. Asked for work/writing balance tips. Possibly writing screenplays or script-adjacent work; not confirmed.
- Met Michael at Montserrat Writers' Festival (Jan 15, 2024). They exchange script editing tips weekly. User worried it's not enough; asked how to get more from it. Advice given: structure the exchange (share specific pages with a focus question), ask "why" not just "what," pair feedback with new drafting, and track what each of them learns.
- Context (2024-03-03): Joseph (fellow producer) peer review sessions started Feb 20; user reports ~15% draft improvement (method unknown). Amy (met Feb 5 at East Janethaven Library) recommended Grammarly Premium; user trying free trial first.
- Goals: 5,000-word screenplay draft by Apr 15, 2024; 1,200 words/week target; tracking in Google Sheet with Google Docs word count.
- Schedule: Mon/Wed/Fri 7 PM, 2-hr sessions, home office.
- Session April 10, 2024: user worried about writing momentum. Says Amy ran a Zoom peer review on April 5, 2024 and user saw a 25% gain in dialogue clarity (method for measuring unknown; earlier Joseph figure was 15%). Not confirmed in memory beyond the user's report. Anxiety about progress again. Gave plan: check current word count vs 5,000-word goal (due April 15, 2024); use remaining Mon/Wed/Fri 7 PM sessions (April 10, April 12, April 15); turn Amy's notes into a dialogue checklist; read dialogue aloud; schedule next peer review.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, same day): user accepted the plan. Plans to continue peer reviews with Amy and others, set goals per session, keep Mon/Wed/Fri schedule. Tools: Grammarly, Hemingway, possibly ProWritingAid again; tracking in Google Docs and Scrivener. Experimenting with tones and revising regularly.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, later): user met Megan at Montserrat Creative Hub on March 28, 2024, who recommended ProWritingAid (trial). User unsure whether to pay given budget and deadline. Asked for pros/cons. Budget figure not confirmed for this decision.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, later still): user says Carla shared an editing checklist on April 7, 2024 and user cut passive voice by 18%. Not in memory beyond user's report. User worried it's not enough. Decided to stick with Grammarly and Hemingway; ProWritingAid deferred until after the project.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, latest): user completed first screenplay draft on April 1, 2024; self-rated confidence rose from 4 to 7 out of 10. Asked what to do next to keep momentum. User chose to tackle passive-voice revisions alone using Carla's checklist.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, deadline update): user now worried about an April 20, 2024 deadline to submit a peer-reviewed draft to the local writing group. Wants to prioritize edits to cut wordiness by 15%. No prior record of a 15% wordiness target in my notes. Sessions Mon/Wed/Fri remaining before submission: April 12, April 15, April 17, April 19, 2024.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, challenge): user entered a 30-day editing challenge starting April 2, 2024 (day 9 today; ends about May 1, 2024). User says they are struggling to stay on track and asked for time-management advice. Existing commitments: Mon/Wed/Fri 7 PM sessions, April 20, 2024 writing group submission.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, tone): user reports using Jasper AI on April 3, 2024, which improved tone consistency by 22% (not verified in my notes). Asked what other AI tools could help with tone consistency. Earlier decision still in place: avoid adding tools before the April 20, 2024 submission.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, clarity vs concision): user chose clarity over concision after Amy's suggestion; average sentence length rose 5%. Asked whether that's right for their style. Conflicts somewhat with the 15% wordiness-cut target for the April 20, 2024 submission.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, editor choice): user is weighing AI tools against a freelance editor quoted at $1,200 and worries AI choice could hurt quality. Asked for thoughts. Not yet decided per user.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, hybrid plan): user chose hybrid approach: AI tools for initial edits and basic errors, then a freelance editor for final review. Asked whether to find the editor now. Advice: research and shortlist now, book after revisions lock; the editor reviews a finished draft.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, interruptions): user rescheduled a writing session from April 6, 2024 to April 8, 2024 due to a 3 PM production meeting on Main Street. Asked whether deadlines are still reachable with interruptions. Also started looking for a freelance editor (Upwork, Reedsy, referrals from Amy and Carla).
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, Megan): user declined a collaboration request from Megan (met March 28, 2024 at Montserrat Creative Hub) on April 9, 2024, and worries it will affect the relationship. Asked whether they should have explained workload more clearly.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, AI vs manual): user prefers AI-assisted tools for tone calibration (Jasper used April 3, 2024) and asked for pros/cons versus manual revision for time savings on a solo project. Reviewed and suggested a short reply to Megan (declined collaboration; deadline April 20, 2024); user adopted a revised version.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, webinar): user is worried about applying skills from an "Advanced Editing Techniques" webinar hosted by Montserrat Writers' Guild on April 12, 2024. That date is after today (April 10), so the user hasn't attended yet; I don't know its content. Asked for practice help. Conflicts with the Friday April 12, 2024 writing session.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, pace): weekly word count rose from 1,200 to 1,500 by April 9, 2024 (tracked in Google Docs). User unsure if pace is sustainable. Note: upcoming 15% cut will lower the total, so track new words separately from net count.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, voice metric): user asked about impact of "active voice in 40% of sentences" vs 25% in first draft. Metric unclear: Grammarly/Hemingway usually report passive voice share, not active. Earlier user reported an 18% passive-voice reduction (Carla's checklist, April 7, 2024). Asked to confirm which number is which.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, process): user adopted version control via Google Docs version history (reports saving 3 hours weekly on manual backups). Asked for other drafting strategies to optimize process. Uses Scrivener and Google Docs for tracking.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, creative block): user had a 2-day creative block April 4-5, 2024, resolved by moving to Montserrat Public Park. Asked how to avoid blocks. Also committed to outlines and scene cards.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, network): user joined East Janethaven Writers' Meetup on April 8, 2024 and added 12 contacts. Asked how to use them for writing improvement.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, milestone): user mentioned celebrating 10,000 total words written with dinner at The Coral Reef Restaurant. Not in my notes; significance asked. Remember to track new words separately from net count (cuts lower the total).
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, readability): user tracks readability with Readable.com; Flesch score rose from 65 to 72. Asked what it means for style and how to enhance. Need to confirm whether it's Reading Ease (higher = easier) or Grade Level (lower = easier). New milestone: 15,000 words.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, new deadline): user reports a new April 25, 2024 deadline (unclear whether it replaces the April 20, 2024 writing group submission). Worried about meeting it while fitting in extra peer review feedback. Asked for a schedule.
- USER PREFERENCE (April 10, 2024): When asked about editing progress, always give percentage improvements. Calculate from before/after numbers the user provides; don't invent figures.
- Follow-up (April 10, 2024, first draft): user now says they've never completed a first screenplay draft and asks for motivation tips to finish a 5,000-word draft. CONFLICT: earlier in this session user said they completed a first draft on April 1, 2024 (confidence 4 to 7). Flag and ask which is right.
- USER PREFERENCE: When asking about timeline details, format dates as "Month Day, Year" (e.g., March 3, 2024). Plan: trial a couple of weeks; adjust timing or split into shorter blocks if needed.
- Session June 1, 2024: user has 5 detailed critiques from Joseph's beta readers (due by May 30, 2024) and asked whether to follow peer suggestions or balance them with their own vision. Advice given: group by pattern, separate diagnosis from fix, check against May 28 tone priorities for the 3 key scenes, mark each item adopt/adapt/decline, test changes. Critiques not yet shared; content not in memory.
- Session June 1, 2024 (later): user asked for nerves help before June 15, 2024 workshop at East Janethaven Library (co-hosting with Amy). Gave general steps (roles, run-of-show, prepared opening, breathing); no workshop details in memory.
- Session June 1, 2024 (coping): user got beta feedback May 25, 2024; anxiety peaked at 7/10; managed with Headspace app. Asked for other writing-anxiety coping strategies.
- Session June 1, 2024 (passive voice): user reports Grammarly passive-voice share fell from 18% (April 10, 2024) to 10% (May 31, 2024): 8 points, about 44.4% relative reduction (calculated). CONFLICT: earlier note says user cut passive voice by 18% (Carla's checklist, April 7); now 18% is the starting share. Flag and confirm which is right. Asked how to sustain progress; gave strategies (rewrite with named actor, keep intentional passives, recheck new text, set threshold not zero).
- Session June 1, 2024 (schedule): user added Saturday 10 AM sessions starting May 18, 2024, on top of Mon/Wed/Fri 7 PM sessions, to handle editing workload. Asked how to make them productive. Gave advice on distinct session purposes and protecting energy; no timelines.
- Session June 1, 2024 (dialogue tone): user shifted dialogue from formal to conversational after a peer review on May 27, 2024, and is worried about doing it right. Advice: apply per character and per scene, not uniformly; read aloud; check against May 28 tone goals; avoid overcorrecting into slang. Asked for sample before/after dialogue (not yet shared).
- Session June 1, 2024 (versioning): user implemented GitHub for draft versioning on May 22, 2024, tracking 15 major revisions. Earlier notes (April 10, 2024) record Google Docs version history as the versioning method, so both may now be in use. Asked how to use version control to improve writing; advice on commits, tags for critique rounds, branches for tone variants, and word-diffs for passive-voice regressions.
- Session June 1, 2024 (Michael review): user set a 1-hour limit for Michael (met at Montserrat Writers' Festival, Jan 15, 2024; weekly script exchange) to review their script on May 29, 2024, and worries it's not enough time. Gave a structure: send pages ahead, focus question, agree on scope, timer, follow-up notes. Unclear whether the May 29 review already happened; asked.
- Session June 1, 2024 (missed session): user missed a May 23, 2024 session due to a 2 PM production meeting at Montserrat Studios, made up 4 hours of editing May 24-25, and asked whether to prioritize writing over meetings. Note: May 23, 2024 was a Thursday, not a listed session day; asked user to confirm what was scheduled. Advice: don't frame as writing vs. work; adjust blocks, protect core sessions, watch load.
- Session June 1, 2024 (budget): user chose self-editing over a $500 copyeditor to stay within a $1,000 monthly budget, and asked if that was right. Note: this departs from the April hybrid plan (AI tools then freelance final review; freelance editor previously quoted $1,200). Advice given: depends on deliverable and deadline; self-editing misses blind spots; consider a targeted copyedit before submission. Asked for deliverable and timing.
- Session June 1, 2024 (quiz): user scored 92% on the final quiz for a Narrative Structure Masterclass on Udemy, completed May 15, 2024, and worried about it. Also asked how to deepen narrative-structure understanding. Also asked about weekend (Saturday) session tips; advice given.
- Session June 1, 2024 (word goal): user reports reaching 20,000 total words by June 1, 2024, described as 33% above an "initial target" of 15,000 (calculated: 5,000 ÷ 15,000 = 33.3%). CONFLICT: earlier notes set the initial goal at 5,000 words (April 15, 2024 deadline) and 15,000 as a later milestone. Confirm which is the baseline. Asked for help setting the next goal; track new words separately from net total.
- Session June 1, 2024 (pacing): user reorganized scenes 4 and 7 on May 26, 2024, reporting a 12% reduction in average scene length; unsure if enough. Unclear whether 12% applies to scenes 4 and 7 only or the whole script (asked). Advice: judge pacing by scene function and reader response, not a fixed percentage.
- Session June 1, 2024 (subplots): user received 3 new subplot suggestions from beta readers, added to outline May 20, 2024, and asked how to balance them with the original vision. Note: May 20 predates the May 25 critique feedback; confirm whether this is a separate round. Subplots added before the May 26 reorganization may be relevant to the pacing concern.
- Session June 1, 2024 (motivation): user rated motivation 8/10 after Amy's invitation (May 30, 2024) and mentions networking with about 30 writers and editors met at the Montserrat Literary Festival on May 18, 2024 (may be a different event from the Montserrat Writers' Festival, Jan 15, 2024). Asked how to sustain motivation. Advice given on routines, network follow-up, and small wins.
- Session June 1, 2024 (network for skills): user asked how to use the May 18 Montserrat Literary Festival network (30 writers and editors) and Amy's June 15, 2024 co-hosted workshop at East Janethaven Library to improve writing and get peer feedback. Advice: pick a few peers for ongoing exchange, offer structured feedback, use the workshop as a two-way feedback opportunity.
- Session June 1, 2024 (clarity challenge): user reports a clarity editing challenge from May 10 to May 25, 2024 (16 calendar days inclusive; user calls it 15) cutting filler words by 20%. Asked how this affects overall writing quality. Advice: check that cuts didn't remove voice or character speech patterns; need before/after counts to calculate.
- Session June 1, 2024 (ProWritingAid): user integrated the ProWritingAid desktop app on May 21, 2024, reporting a 10% grammar-accuracy gain (unverified; no before/after counts given). Earlier note (April 10, 2024) deferred ProWritingAid until after the project. Asked whether it's enough for goals or whether to add resources. Advice: tool covers mechanics, not structure, character, or tone; pair with beta readers, a final copyedit, and craft study.
- Session June 1, 2024 (beta management): user asked how to manage feedback from 7 beta readers, saying they have never attended a literary festival or networking event. CONFLICT: earlier sessions record attending the Montserrat Literary Festival on May 18, 2024 (30 contacts), and the beta critiques were earlier counted as 5. Flag both; ask which is right.
- USER PREFERENCE (June 1, 2024, restated): always include specific dates for event timelines, formatted "Month Day, Year" (e.g., May 18, 2024). Applies to all future timeline answers.
- Session June 1, 2024 (first draft): user says they have never completed a first screenplay draft, while asking how to apply self-editing skills. CONFLICT (third time): April 1, 2024 first draft completed per April 10 notes; the same session flagged it. Also the user has discussed revising scenes 4 and 7, three key scenes, and beta critiques of a script. Asked which is right; advice: draft first with editing deferred, then apply the self-editing system.
